name: Macfos Limited
summary:
Macfos is a genuine organic electronics-distribution and fulfilment business with an effective digital storefront, not simply a software platform and not a contractor. Its stocked catalogue, sourcing, local delivery and technical help remove real procurement friction for engineers, manufacturers and hobbyists. Revenue grew from ₹27.12 crore in FY21 to ₹308.77 crore in FY26, while gross profit reached ₹71.68 crore. An organic multi-year incremental-capital bridge supports economically useful reinvestment even after including supplier advances and deposits. Those strengths should not be erased merely because it sells physical goods.

The decisive reservation is cash and funding visibility, not a presumption of fraud or an invented lack of business quality. Five-year cumulative CFO is negative, inventory and supplier advances have expanded sharply, and the latest quarter does not disclose enough balance-sheet detail to bridge that expansion to available cash and bank headroom. October CRISIL BBB/Stable and its adequate-liquidity view are important counterevidence, but ₹13.567 crore of >12-month bank deposits cannot be silently treated as immediately spendable cash.

At the secondary ₹1,010 close on 19 October 2026, market value is ₹1,046.21 crore. BQS is 6.16; raw GQS 7.25 is capped at 5.00 for persistent poor cash realization. IAS is NS, because prospective return and liquidity are unverified. Classification: Hold — unresolved, with attractive operating execution but material funding/valuation sensitivity. This is an analytical conclusion, not advice to transact.

sections.title: Research header, identity, scope and gates
sections.text:
Exact legal/security identity is Macfos Limited, CIN L29309PN2017PLC172718, ISIN INE0OLH01013, BSE SME code 543787 and ticker ROBU. The official 19 October security master identifies ROBU$, SM, 10358503 issued shares and 165-share lot. The dated ₹1010 close is corroborated secondary history, not a current executable offer. Three lots, 495 shares, cost ₹499950; four lots cost ₹666600. The ₹5 lakh reference is a liquidity convention, not a proposed allocation.

The six observations required for FY21–26 CAGR are available; FY20 adds context. FY20–22 use IPO-restated standalone numbers, FY23 statutory standalone, FY24–26 consolidated. Subsidiaries are economically tiny: FY26 consolidated sales exceed standalone by only ₹.0249 crore. No material acquired-revenue jump supports the growth score. FY26 annual statements use Accounting Standards/Indian GAAP; Q1FY27 voluntarily adopts Ind AS. TTM construction uses converted Ind AS comparatives, never an unmarked AS/Ind AS splice.

Forecast investment dates are 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031. Nominal pretax equity hurdle 15% has 12%/18% sensitivities. G1/G2 are Conditional, G3/G4 Hold — unresolved. sections.title: Scorecard, weights and uncertainty
sections.text:
Factors: GOV 6, MOAT 6, REV 9, DUR 7, CAP 6, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 7, EARN 7; R NS, D 3, P 4, L NS. Exact Decimal BQS contributions are GOV 1.20 + MOAT 1.20 + REV 1.08 + DUR.70 + CAP.72 + CASH.30 + BAL.40 + EXEC.56 =6.16. GQS is REV 3.60 + DUR 1.40 + EARN 1.05 + CAP.90 + CASH.30 =7.25 before the explicit cap 5.00. CASH 3 is justified by persistent multi-year operating realization, not merely a transitory working-capital build or high capital expenditure.

IAS reuses unrounded BQS: Q1.5400 + D.60 + P.40 =known 2.5400 at 55% coverage. Missing R 35% and L 10% produce mathematical bounds 2.99–7.04, not a point, probability interval or ranking. No guessed neutral factors are used. BQS/GQS are complete quality assessments only; unresolved investment gates prevent an investability conclusion. The 13 factor audits each preserve two material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and locators.

Judgment sensitivity: MOAT±1 moves BQS±.20; CAP±1 moves BQS±.12 and raw GQS±.15; BAL±1 moves BQS±.08; EARN±1 moves raw GQS±.15. The GQS cap remains binding under these individual changes. If future evidence shows CASH weakness was genuinely temporary and conversion normalizes, lifting the cap requires a revised evidence-based CASH assessment, not simply re-labeling inventory as platform investment.

sections.title: Business model, customer economics and moat
sections.text:
Robu.in is principally an inventory-owning distributor with digital customer acquisition, small-order fulfilment, sourcing and technical assistance. Components, sensors, motors, robotics/drone parts, development boards and related electronics reach both corporate/institutional and individual users. Purchased goods and inventory movements dominate cost of sales; no evidence supports valuing gross merchandise sales as high-margin software net revenue. Assembly, own brands and technical services may increase value capture, but their separately audited profits and capital economics are unavailable.

Catalogue breadth and fast local availability have genuine economic value: customers avoid fragmented supplier discovery, import/payment friction and coordinating many small orders. Repeated execution and procurement scale can create a useful process advantage even without contractual switching. Nevertheless, a catalogue is not automatically a network effect: adding low-value passive SKUs does not guarantee demand, exclusivity or greater profit per customer. CRISIL describes exclusive distributorships; scope and duration were not independently verified with vendors/contracts. Management also tempers the importance of partnerships in the April call.

FY25 customer count was corrected from 182647 to 145231 after duplicate entries; FY26 is 185059. Orders increased 396366→505250. These are management KPIs, not audited cohorts. Repeat orders are qualitatively reported but customer retention, repeat gross profit, acquisition cost/payback, LTV/CAC and private-brand segment profits are ND. Q1 orders grew 4.9%, customers 12.9%, AOV 30.8%; revenue strength therefore cannot be described as equivalent unit-volume growth. Visitors are especially method-sensitive. MOAT 6 recognizes practical service differentiation while withholding a structural-moat premium.

sections.title: Industry, competitive position and demand runway
sections.text:
Electronics prototyping, automation, robotics, manufacturing, education and small-batch product development offer multiple routes to demand. Macfos already serves these markets rather than merely citing their TAM. More reliable sourcing and broader availability may expand wallet share as domestic design/manufacturing develops. Accessible demand is not guaranteed profitable demand: imported product availability, currency movements, export/import rules, counterfeit/product-quality controls, technology obsolescence and customer willingness to pay for service all matter. No unsupported industry-growth percentage or market-share estimate is inserted.

Three economic comparators frame the opportunity. RS Group is a mature high-service industrial/electronics distributor with FY26 adjusted operating margin 9.2%, ROCE 15.4% and adjusted operating cash conversion 109.1%. Its inventory-provision and working-capital reporting show that catalogue service still requires cash discipline. Its geography, customer mix, acquisitions and accounting differ, so its operating statistics are context, not a direct multiple. DigiKey's dated Q1 release distinguishes nearly 31000 added stocking parts from 387000 products made available to order: listed catalogue is not stocked availability. Mouser added 63 manufacturer partners in 2025 and works with more than 1200 manufacturers. Both private competitors have deep sourcing and technical resources; no financial multiples are fabricated for them.

Macfos may have local price/service and small-order advantages without matching their global scale. Domestic specialists and direct supplier channels remain competition. DUR 7 rests on existing channels and repeatable adjacent product opportunities, not an assumption that robotics branding guarantees proprietary technology or limitless margins.

sections.title: Historical financial record and growth quality
sections.text:
Revenue FY20–26 was 16.2181,27.1192,55.5147,80.1682,125.1331,255.0614 and 308.7733 crore. The selected FY21–26 CAGR is 62.6569%; FY23–26 is 56.7518%; FY20–26 is 63.4080%. Ten-year CAGR is ND because the required history is unavailable. The growth score starts 9 under the framework and receives no adjustment. FY25's approximately ₹71 crore one-off bulk business explains much of its unusual sales base and lower margin; the management ex-bulk FY26 growth proxy 67.76% is shown separately, never substituted opportunistically for the chosen five-year window.

Gross profit rose ₹21.7855 crore FY23 to ₹71.6770 crore FY26, supporting growth in value added rather than only pass-through sales. FY26 gross margin 23.21% compares with 18.66% FY25. Operating EBITDA excluding all other income increased ₹24.4346→₹36.1374 crore, margin 9.58%→11.70%. The presentation's ₹39.13 crore includes other income and is not the normalized operating denominator. FY26 finance cost 3.1347 and D&A 1.6304 are retained separately. PAT 25.6396 exceeds 17.9194, while current-share-equivalent and reported bonus-adjusted EPS are clearly separated.

Q1FY27 consolidated revenue 81.3401 versus 59.2680 crore is+37.24%; PAT 5.8116 versus converted 4.9615 is+17.13%. Q1 is not extrapolated as a full-year cash run rate. Indicative comparable Ind AS TTM revenue 330.8454 and PAT 26.4507 use FY26 Ind AS 25.6006, plus current quarter, less converted prior quarter. TTM CFO is ND. Full historical rows include tax-basis normalization, margins, debt/cash, capital, working-capital days and source scope. Small entity scale is a risk context, not a second numerical penalty on an already valid CAGR.

sections.title: Earnings-to-cash, inventory and forensic reconciliation
sections.text:
FY26 profit is real in the audited accounts, but operating cash conversion remains poor. CFO−7.9985 crore plus cash capex 2.5149 gives FCF proxy−10.5134 before financing-interest cash. FY25 CFO was−22.7628 on the latest comparative basis; original−24.5969 is preserved rather than overwritten. Three-year cumulative CFO/PAT is−.4921× and five-year−.3206×. Inventory increased ₹23.9729 crore, supplier advances ₹16.9740 crore and receivables ₹7.5597 crore during FY26; payables increased ₹6.3919 crore. Those investments can generate future service revenue, but capital expenditure itself does not cause negative CFO.

March 2026 stock 79.5715 and supplier advances 29.4997 total ₹109.0712 crore, substantially exceeding net fixed assets. Receivable days are comparatively modest, so this is more an assortment/procurement cash cycle than a contractor-style collection/retention story. Management reports slow stock >9 months 6.21%, up from 2.64%, then 5.52% inJune. This is not an audited liquidation-value guarantee. FY26 return/replacement costs 1.0989 crore rose versus.5819; some can be service quality investment, but sustained increases would hurt contribution profit. The stress case charges 5% inventory replacement cash once, not merely a noncash accounting write-off.

FY24 CFO 5.0032→3.9969 is offset by+1.0063 cash-FX classification. FY25 CFO−24.5969→−22.7628 is offset by−1.8341 cash-FX; provision regrouping additionally reconciles presentation subtotals. Closing cash remains unchanged. May 12's inventory/receivable line-position correction is a distinct clerical event. The rebuilt FY24 cash bridge uses visually checked CFI−5.7746 and CFF.3191, giving closing.6816 exactly. No unexplained material cash creation remains; repeated corrections still warrant care.

sections.title: Governance, audit scope and accounting reliability
sections.text:
The statutory audit review goes beyond the main opinion. FY25 standalone CARO and separate internal-control report were inspected in full. FY26 standalone main audit refers to CARO Annexure 1 and IFC Annexure 2, but those annexures are absent from the retrieved annual-report package and were not found in the corrected annual-results attachment. This is recorded as missing, not silently called clean. FY26 consolidated audit explicitly reports no adverse CARO remarks and gives a clean IFC opinion. Parent and Indian subsidiary audit-trail reporting is clean; the tiny foreign subsidiary's scope exception is not evidence of a material audit-trail failure.

Bank stock/debtor reporting is not ignored. FY25 maximum absolute disclosed difference is ₹.1913 crore, explained as debtor timing. FY26 December bank return 91.8476 versus books 92.8901 is bridged by 1.0424 crore valuation difference, with.0001 crore rounding; other quarters, including March, agree. The adjustment is about 1.12% of that asset return and 1.09% of FY26 equity, not immaterial by assertion, yet bounded rather than an unquantified balance-sheet hole. The company explanation is preserved; SKU-level independent revaluation is unavailable.

First-quarter Ind AS reporting explicitly says converted comparative quarters were not reviewed. FY26 special-purpose Ind AS audit dated 11 August is referenced but not separately retrieved. Reconciliation is small and quantified: AS PAT 25.6396→Ind AS 25.6006, plus OCI−.1652 produces TCI 25.4354. Lease−.2551, deposit interest+.0545, lease-land depreciation−.0715, other+.0341 and deferred tax+.0338 sum−.2042. Thus no material unexplained transition is presumed; valuation stays on cash-rent economics.

Promoters control 69.10%. Audited remuneration totals ₹1.611 crore versus 1.08,+49.17%, whereas the narrative annexure reports 3.52% for each promoter; no reconciliation found. September AGM disclosure exceeded 12 hours; the company attributes delay to an OTP issue, not independently verified. RPTs mainly include remuneration, small promoter loans and subsidiaries; intercompany flows are eliminated in consolidated analysis. These concerns support GOV 6 and Conditional G1/G2, not an accusation of diversion.

sections.title: Capital allocation and organic incremental returns
sections.text:
Do not mistake low fixed assets for zero capital needs or negative CFO for proof of bad reinvestment. Macfos needs inventory, supplier advances, deposits and a cash buffer to provide its service. The stable organic perimeter permits a meaningful aggregate incremental-return substitute even without private cohorts. Financing invested capital is equity plus interest-bearing debt less cash and separately excluded long FDs, then adds required cash max ₹2 crore/2% sales. Direct operating-capital construction independently includes inventory, receivables, supplier/operating advances and deposits, less non-interest operating liabilities, plus net fixed assets. Differences reflect taxes/provisions, not a claim that every rupee is excess.

Using operating EBIT excluding other income and 25% normalized tax, FY23–26 ΔNOPAT ₹18.0598 crore divided by Δcapital ₹99.4231 crore gives 18.16%. FY22–26 gives 18.24%; FY24–26 gives 16.37%; FY25–26 gives 20.68%. Keeping all incremental long FDs lowers these to 16.27%,16.07%,14.89% and 19.83%, respectively. The 13–16% cost-of-capital range is an analyst risk convention, not observed market pricing. Mixed results near its upper end justify CAP 6. They do not establish extraordinary returns, but support productive distribution growth rather than an automatic NS or destructive-investment label.

FY25 equity issue 581397 shares at ₹430 raised ₹25.000071 crore; share count grew 6.58%, old-holder dilution 6.17%. The 2023 IPO was entirely offer-for-sale, so issuer growth proceeds were zero. March 2026 bonus 1:10 adds 941682 shares to 10358503 and does not dilute economic ownership. Existing asset turnover and current ROCE are cross-checks, not the sole CAP evidence. Further improvement requires ageing discipline, evidence supplier advances convert promptly, and durable contribution profit on the expanded catalogue; segment/cohort ROIC remains ND. The dated promises-versus-delivery register separately tests the 30 April own-brand, spare-capacity and inventory-optimization aims against 11 August evidence: product-development activity is visible, spare-capacity utilization is unverified, and slow-stock percentage improved while total stock still absorbed cash. These were not fixed dated revenue/turn guarantees, so unresolved delivery is not mislabeled a missed deadline.

sections.title: Funding, cash availability and obligation bridge
sections.text:
March 2026 consolidated liquid cash ₹1.8325 crore is separate from ₹13.567 crore bank deposits with remaining maturity beyond 12 months. Their sum ₹15.3995 crore reconciles CRISIL's rounded ₹15.39 crore, so there is no cash contradiction. Breakability, lien status and current availability of those deposits are not established. Total debt 36.0193 comprises CC 34.8838, term 1.0833 and related-party.0522. October 1 rated facilities 40 crore include actual CC 37.3 and proposed 2.7; proposed finance is not available money. Nominal headroom against March drawings is 2.4162, not current confirmed headroom. CRISIL's 80% average usage over 12 months throughJune and adequate-liquidity view indicate access, not today's balance.

Term repayment around ₹.50–.55 crore annually is modest against rating cash-accrual expectations above ₹27 crore. However accrual before working capital is not CFO. Q1 inventory increased ₹17.9136 crore and supplier-advance conversion/current drawings were not disclosed. This gap is the specific reason current funding is unresolved. A supplier-advance release or breakable FD could resolve it, but neither is inserted as established cash. G3 Hold is not a default prediction, and no private daily bank statement is mechanically demanded: sufficiently current published balances and an evidenced conservative obligations bridge would suffice.

The analytical reserve max ₹2 crore/2% sales creates a March opening deficit ₹1.9268 crore even after all nominal CC headroom; a flat ₹2 crore or 1% reserve does not. This sensitivity prevents the assumed buffer from masquerading as a contractual breach. Annual models also do not prove intraperiod financeability. Tax/advance-tax net ₹1.1338 plus tax interest.0923 is charged once, employee claims.9684 deducted once at terminal, and small related debt repaid. The contingent note has an inconsistent bills-discounting label alongside customs-notice narrative:₹.5243 is stressed once without asserting two additive claims. Future cash-rent commitments 2.3374 within a year and 9.0753 in years 2–5 are included through after-rent margins, not double-counted as lease debt. No operational property is added separately.

sections.title: Valuation, cash scenarios and rescue diagnostics
sections.text:
Reference market capitalization ₹1,046.21 crore implies FY26 AS P/E40.80×, Ind AS P/E40.87×, price/book 10.91× and cash-rent EV/EBITDA 29.90×. These combine the dated secondary share price with March balances; they are not current enterprise value precision. Long FDs are excluded from near-term liquidity and shown only as explicit eventual recovery value.

Bear/base/bull assume growth 8%/20%/30%, operating EBITDA after cash rent 8%/11%/12.5%, ONWC/sales 40%/33.95%/32%, capex 1.2%/1.2%/1.5%, D&A.6% and exit multiples 12×/20×/28×. No rerating is required in the base, but a 20× exit still assumes enduring quality. Pre-entry March 31→October 19 and all investor stubs use actual fiscal-day fractions, including leap-year days. Only existing 37.3 crore CC capacity is modeled, no proposed facility or automatic FD release. Net operating capital, taxes, capex, interest, principal and cash reserves remain linked.

Annual ratio-path peak unmet cash needs are ₹24.60/₹2.32/₹4.30 crore. Separate observed-Q1 no-advance-release stress is ₹38.99/₹11.43/₹9.09 crore. These are annual diagnostics, not proven maximum intraday needs; earlier inventory timing could be worse. Same-period incremental CC interest is separately bounded, not silently treated as fully modeled.

All ordinary returns and entry prices remain null. Conditional non-rescue and rescue returns also remain null because opening/intraperiod funding is not established, even when a year-end path looks positive. Separate rescue uses ₹600 issue price, 2% fees and integer-ceiling shares to size period-end cash gaps; gross/fees/net/new shares/holder dilution are explicit. Such issuance is not asserted available, approved or properly prefunded. Signed negative cash remains a deficit in terminal equity, not invented debt. Required cash, debt and employee claims are deducted once. Terminal prices are non-investable algebra, never targets.

sections.title: Sensitivities, reverse expectations and capital impairment
sections.text:
The complete model includes growth 10–30% versus 12–28× exit multiple; ONWC 32–45% versus EBITDA margin 8–12.5%; 12/15/18% equity hurdles; 0/50/100% long-FD recovery haircuts; and 0/1/2/3% reserve-ratio diagnostics. Separate CC non-renewal and double-capex paths retain all annual rows and cash gaps. Revenue growth can increase cash needs before creating distributable value, so the bull case is not automatically safest. Slower growth may release capital mathematically but cannot guarantee older stock converts at book value. A realistic downside couples weaker gross margin, slow-stock replacement, funding limits and lower exit valuation rather than changing only the multiple.

Reverse expectations do not report a fictitious funded growth solution. The 0–60% growth scan has no verified investable crossing because opening/current financeability is unresolved. A bare algebraic terminal-price crossing is not a return hurdle solution. At ₹1010, a 15% five-year hurdle requires about ₹2031 terminal value per existing share before investor tax and any rescue dilution. The base 20% growth/11% margin/20× exit diagnostic falls short even before establishing financeability; historical growth above 20% is credible counterevidence, not permission to ignore capital requirements.

DCF is a conditional cross-check, not a target. Explicit after-cash-rent FCFF deducts incremental ONWC, net capex and growth in required operating cash. Terminal ROIC 18% is defined on incremental capital INCLUDING required cash; g/ROIC reinvestment therefore includes reserve growth. WACC 12/14/16/18% and terminal growth 3/4/5% show terminal-value dependence. The signed entry cash minus reserve is retained. Long deposits are an assumed recovery on 19 October 2031 discounted back five years at the tested discount rate, never current funding. Recovery haircuts of 0/50/100% are separately tested; timing/liens can lower value further. A lack of funded model outputs is not proof the shares are worthless, but prevents a defensible R/IAS point. D 3 reflects credible material impairment/recapitalization risk at this valuation.

The 14% WACC/4% terminal-growth DCF gives about ₹260 per share as non-investable algebra, with about 92% of operating value terminal. This is far below the 20× EBITDA exit convention: the DCF assumes mature 4% growth, 18% incremental ROIC and continuing reinvestment, implying about 5.74× terminal EBITDA. A 20× terminal multiple implicitly requires premium growth/economics beyond the explicit five years. These are alternative duration assumptions, not two mutually confirming fair values. The divergence is a valuation warning supporting P 4, not a reason to discard the lower cross-check.

sections.title: Market microstructure and implementation limits
sections.text:
The 165-share lot is approximately ₹166650 at the dated reference. The illustrative ₹5 lakh position rounds down to 3 lots/495 shares/₹499950, not fractional shares. Four lots cost ₹666600. Promoter 69.10% leaves a 30.90% public-holding proxy, not guaranteed executable free float.

Sixty secondary observed rows 24 July–19 October give close×volume mean ₹63.25 lakh and median ₹49.30 lakh. The 20-row window 21 September–19 October gives mean ₹34.80 lakh and median ₹29.40 lakh. These are turnover proxies, not official rupee traded values. At the more conservative 60-row mean/median, 2%/5%/10% participation yields fractional ₹5 lakh exit diagnostics 5.07/2.03/1.01 days. At 5%, median whole-lot capacity is 1 lot in 60 rows but 0 lots in 20 rows; only 8 of the latest 20 observed days allow at least one lot at that participation limit. Thus a smooth average obscures practical trading constraints.

Observed rows contain no zero-volume prints, but that does not establish zero missing/no-trade sessions. Invalid HTML/403 archive responses are not trading data; absence of a BSE issuer in NSE daily data is not a zero. Official traded values and issuer calendar authentication, current spread/depth, circuit queues and decoded restriction clearance are unavailable. No claim of unrestricted or guaranteed execution is made. L stays NS and G4 Hold — unresolved. Recheck the actual position and live microstructure before any implementation analysis.

sections.title: Fivefold/tenfold outcome test and monitoring
sections.text:
Fivefold price appreciation over five years requires 37.97% annualized; tenfold requires 58.49%. With unchanged shares and no dividend, market capitalization would need to rise from about ₹1046.21 crore to ₹5231.04/₹10462.09 crore. This is not a forecast. At 20× after-rent EBITDA and 11% operating margin, even ignoring net financial claims, those values imply roughly ₹2378/₹4756 crore annual revenue. At 28× and 12.5% margin, the corresponding gross-equity simplification still needs ₹1495/₹2989 crore. Debt, reserves and dilution make equity requirements harder; no funded 5×/10× path is established.

Monitor quarterly order counts and AOV separately, gross profit rather than only gross sales, contribution margin after fulfilment/returns, repeat-order cohorts if disclosed, inventory aging and provisions, supplier-advance conversion, and CFO after taxes and interest. A meaningful positive catalyst would be a published cash/credit/FD bridge and conversion of the expanded catalogue into cash without repeated equity raises, not simply another SKU milestone. Repeated profits without conversion, higher aged stock, unexplained bank-return differences, additional dilutive finance or worsening related-party disclosure would weaken the case.

Revisit after the next comparable results with a balance sheet and cash flow, fresh rating/facility details, and the missing audit packs. Require 0 unexplained material cash/Ind AS bridges, capital returns robust above cost of capital, and liquidity evidence at the real position. A lower price alone does not resolve survival or execution uncertainty. No future regulatory/listing migration or vendor exclusivity is assumed approved solely because management discusses it.

sections.title: Evidence gaps, falsification conditions and conclusion
sections.text:
What would change the conclusion: evidenced current liquid resources, confirmed drawable credit and advance conversion sufficient for a conservative stress bridge could clear G3 and enable ordinary scenario returns. Complete official issuer trading history and live restrictions/spread/lot evidence could enable L. Robust incremental return after inventory provision/FD-retention sensitivity and multi-year positive operating conversion would support a stronger quality score. Independently documented repeat economics or durable vendor/customer switching advantages could raise MOAT; a larger catalogue or brand claim alone would not.

Remaining gaps are explicit: FY26 standalone CARO/IFC annexures and separate 11 August Ind AS audit; remuneration percentage reconciliation; FD breakability/liens; June/current cash, debt and supplier advances; cohort retention/LTV-CAC; brand/service segment contribution returns; full current ownership/pledge verification; and executable official market microstructure. These are not all equally material. Quantitatively bounded audit/comparability gaps do not automatically force G2 Hold, whereas current funding remains decision-critical. No default, fraud, contract exclusivity or future 10× result is claimed.
